title: 2019 AMC 10A Problem 4
statement: A box contains \(28\) red balls, \(20\) green balls, \(19\) yellow balls, \(13\) blue balls, \(11\) white balls, and \(9\) black balls. What is the minimum number of balls that must be drawn from the box without replacement to guarantee that at least \(15\) balls of a single color will be drawn?

solutions.text:
Note that we can pull as many as \(14\) balls of each color without ensuring that \(15\) balls of one color are drawn.

This means that we can draw all of the black, white and blue balls, along with \(14\) red, green, and yellow balls.

This gives us a total of \[ 9 + 11 + 13 + 3 \cdot 14 \]\[= 33 + 42 \]\[= 75. \] We need to add one at the end, however, to ensure that we get that \(15\)th ball of some color, \(75 + 1 = 76.\)

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: To avoid getting \(15\) of a color, draw at most \(14\) from each large color
For colors with fewer than \(15\), all of that color can be drawn
